clue.text: In anger, I show spirit

indicators.note: the clue sets the letter I inside the word for anger

parts.note: wrath is great anger

explanation.surface: Someone in a fury shows plenty of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A wraith is a ghost, a spirit of the dead.

clue.text: Almost soaked getting up-river, one's disturbingly transformed

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: wet means soaked

indicators.note: up means the river word is read upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a flower is a cryptic word for a river, something that flows

explanation.surface: A drenched creature heads upstream, transformed horribly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'river' as FLOWER (that which flows) is a crossword favourite; 'up' turns it to REWOLF.
explanation.definitionFit: A werewolf is a person who undergoes a horrifying change into a wolf.

clue.text: One played at one's peak

parts.note: seems to be an athlete at their best; actually an instrument blown on a mountain top

explanation.surface: A player chosen while at their best.
explanation.definitionFit: The alphorn is a long wooden horn played by herders in the Alps.

clue.text: Played winning card in court, against such a charge?

definitions.note: describes the charge, so it stands for an adjective

parts.note: to trump is to play a winning trump card
up means before a court

explanation.surface: A card player accused in court of cheating.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumped-up charge is fabricated, invented falsely.

clue.text: Like monk, old and stooped, about to peg out?

indicators.note: the word for stooped goes around the phrase for dying

parts.note: a stooped person is bent
to peg out is slang for to die

explanation.surface: An aged, bowed monk is near death.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks take a vow of obedience, so dutiful submission is monkish.

clue.text: Warning on packet: not so good when taken out?

definitions.meaning: a label advising when food should be eaten by

definitions.text: not so good when taken out?
definitions.meaning: food is less good when taken from a packet after this point

explanation.definitionFit: A best-before date is the printed limit for food quality.

clue.text: Cheats, adding penny into subscriptions

indicators.note: the penny letter goes into the subscriptions word

parts.note: dues are subscriptions paid

explanation.surface: Fraudsters slipping an extra penny into membership fees.
explanation.definitionFit: To dupe is to cheat or trick someone.

clue.text: Queries mistaken title

indicators.note: mistaken means the letters have gone wrong, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Questions about an incorrect form of address.
explanation.definitionFit: Esquire is a courtesy title written after a man's name.

clue.text: Organised criminals brought to book across border

indicators.note: across means the other letters lie across the border word, around it

parts.note: a hem is a border on cloth

explanation.surface: Gangsters prosecuted across a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mob is a name for the Mafia or organised crime.

clue.text: Film star cried, not working — it was US policy

parts.note: Marilyn Monroe was a film star

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: A movie star cried and stopped work during an era of American policy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not working' looks like 'idle'; here only 'working' signals the anagram, of CRIED and NOT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Monroe Doctrine was the 1823 US foreign policy opposing European colonialism in the Americas.

clue.text: Wildly soar up, holding back depression, so?

definitions.text: Wildly soar up, holding back depression, so?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters hold the reversed groove inside them
wild movement signals that these letters are jumbled
back tells us to read the groove word from right to left

parts.note: a rut is a groove or depression in the ground

explanation.surface: Someone whose spirits soar, throwing off their gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wildly' rearranges soar up and 'back' turns the depression word round; 'holding' sets it inside. The whole clue also describes the feeling, so it doubles as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Soaring wildly free of gloom describes an ecstatic, joyous state.

clue.text: Noise from dog causes resentment

indicators.note: noise tells us to go by the sound of the dog's name

parts.note: a peke is a Pekingese dog

explanation.surface: A dog's barking annoys the neighbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Pique is wounded pride or irritated resentment.

clue.text: Lie with a jumper on

parts.note: a hopper is something that hops or jumps

explanation.surface: A false story told while wearing a sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' looks like the British word for a sweater; here it is something that jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A whopper is a colossal untruth, an outrageous lie.

clue.text: Boat's return concealed by old code out east

indicators.note: a boat's return means its word is read backwards

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a type of boat
hid means concealed

explanation.surface: A returning boat carries a secret ancient eastern code.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai code of honour in Japan, the Far East.

clue.text: Ruled not-guilty plea to be returned, in absence of answer

indicators.note: the letter for answer is left out of the result
returned means the plea's word is read backwards

parts.note: pleading not guilty is a denial of the charge

explanation.surface: A judge ruled that the defendant's plea be sent back without reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be returned' turns DENIAL into LAINED; 'in absence of' removes the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled paper is lined paper, marked with straight lines.

clue.text: Compulsory stop to take in waterfall

indicators.note: the word for stop takes the waterfall word inside it

parts.note: to end is to stop
force is a northern English word for a waterfall

explanation.surface: A mandatory halt to visit a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: FORCE, a waterfall in the Lake District and northern England, is less familiar outside Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enforced is imposed and required, hence compulsory.

clue.text: Lift up delicate part of car

parts.note: to rear is to raise or lift up
light means delicate

explanation.surface: Raising a fragile component of a car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rear light is a lamp on the back of a car.

clue.text: Stew perhaps at old frontier

parts.note: wild letters of west, rearranged, can produce the word stew

explanation.surface: A stew eaten on the old frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: the answer read as wordplay, west wildly rearranged, gives STEW, an example of such ('perhaps').
explanation.definitionFit: The Wild West was the American frontier of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Cross-piece replaced in opening

indicators.note: replaced means the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a rood is a cross, especially in a church
a part is a piece

explanation.surface: A crossbar has been swapped in a doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross-piece' reads as one carpentry word but splits into two synonyms, a church cross and a piece, which 'replaced' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapdoor is a hinged opening in a floor or ceiling.

clue.text: Beautiful goddess almost seized by despicable type

indicators.note: the goddess word is held inside the word for a despicable type

parts.note: a rat is a despicable person

indicators.note: almost means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: Diana was the Roman goddess of hunting

explanation.surface: A lovely goddess grabbed by a villain.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiant means glowing with beauty or happiness.

clue.text: Asian road guide to cherish heartily

parts.note: an A-Z is a British street atlas

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle, so its central letters are taken

explanation.surface: A road map to love with all one's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is a London-born brand of street atlas found throughout Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An Azeri is a native of Azerbaijan, a country in Asia.

clue.text: Over this is eastern male I rank highly

definitions.text: Over this is eastern male I rank highly

parts.note: to rate is to rank highly

explanation.surface: An eastern ruler boasts of his own importance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: an emir, an eastern male of high rank, rules over this state.
explanation.definitionFit: An emirate is a state ruled by an emir.

clue.text: Popular chow?

parts.note: hot means popular, in demand
a chow is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: Food that is in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chow' is slang for food and also a dog breed, so the whole clue is a snack.
explanation.definitionFit: A hot dog is a popular sausage snack, slang chow.

clue.text: Unsavoury sailor?

parts.note: salt kept too long might well be unpleasant to taste, and an experienced seaman has a nickname built from that idea

explanation.surface: A disagreeable seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An old salt is an experienced veteran seaman.

clue.text: More than half the old country in deep hole

indicators.note: five of the nine letters are kept, more than half the word

parts.note: Abyssinia is the old name for Ethiopia

explanation.surface: Most of a former nation is in a deep pit.
explanation.definitionFit: An abyss is a very deep chasm or hole.

clue.text: Held back, and ended excluding nobody?

annotationWithheld.why: Held back, and ended excluding nobody? (7): DALLIED is DIED (ended) including ALL; 'excluding nobody' both supplies ALL and signals the insertion, one phrase doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Held back, and ended excluding nobody?

clue.text: Rejected help with lines in book

indicators.note: rejected suggests turning back, so the help word is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help
RY is the abbreviation for railway, lines

explanation.surface: Assistance with lines was turned down in a book.
explanation.definitionFit: A diary is a book recording daily events or appointments.

clue.text: Organise a get-together and tire agent out

indicators.note: out means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Arranging a party wears out an agent.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into a whole, bringing them together.

clue.text: Decline to visit daughter

parts.note: to go to a place is to visit it
seed means offspring, so a daughter

explanation.surface: Refusing to call on one's daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' looks like refuse; here it means to deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to seed is to deteriorate, to decline in condition.

clue.text: Still time to replace first rook taken in capture

indicators.note: the time letter takes the place of the first rook letter

parts.note: to arrest is to capture
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess player still has time to replace a rook taken.
explanation.definitionFit: At rest means motionless, still.
